Definition: to slacken or be feeble; figuratively, to be oppressed
BiblicalUsage: The word names the thin, slack, brought-low condition of a people under judgment. The glory of Jacob grows thin, the rivers dry up, and the psalmist cries that we are brought very low. Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites, and they cried to the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being brought low is often the beginning of prayer. When we are thin and slack in our own strength, we finally cry to the One who can lift us.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
